reviewed_matched_routes.finding: The benchmark exposes a promising multi-orchestrator adapter surface and adversarial/failure tasks, but the seeded leaderboard still contains no published result rows. There is therefore no public matched canonical S2 cell to admit.

CooperBench remains a direct S2 family at its benchmark-defined team boundary. The reviewed upstream head is unchanged; the committed 50-pair flash ablation report still lacks the pinned flash-run logs used to generate it, so no new observation or canonical matched cell is available.

Reviewed cross-framework comparisons either author the coordination organization inside the benchmark or score generic tool/quality/latency/replay behavior without an explicit interaction-generated S2 disturbance. Framework labels therefore do not create native canonical S2 comparability.

Merge-resolution benchmarks can expose conflict difficulty but evaluate a resolver against already-materialized conflicts rather than comparing native coordination relations among multiple canonical S1 systems. They do not form the required S2 matched cell.

Matched fault-injection campaigns across LangGraph, CrewAI and AutoGen primarily evaluate whether review/checking paths detect planted faults. That is not the required inter-S1 disturbance-to-attenuation S2 comparison.

blocking_reason: Two canonical direct S2 observations now exist, but Squad and thClaws are heterogeneous descriptive operational-history surfaces. No reviewed public benchmark currently evaluates two or more canonical systems under one materially matched inter-S1 disturbance definition while preserving each system's native or adapter-preserved S2 path.
reopen_when: MAO-Bench or another multi-orchestrator benchmark publishes recoverable result rows for at least two canonical systems under one direct S2 disturbance definition
CooperBench publishes immutable run artifacts that support a native or adapter-preserved canonical linkage for at least two systems under one matched protocol

two or more canonical S2 systems publish results under the same benchmark version, disturbance, model/configuration, evaluator and execution policy while exercising their own native or adapter-preserved S2 paths
an existing canonical direct observation gains a second materially comparable canonical row through already-public upstream evidence
do_not_reopen_for: another descriptive canonical observation on a heterogeneous operational-history surface
another framework leaderboard whose orchestration topology is benchmark-authored
another generic quality, latency, token, replay or task-success comparison without an explicit inter-S1 disturbance-to-attenuation relation
an Opensiro-operated reproduction or benchmark run
non_claim: This search closure does not score S2 capability, compare Squad against thClaws, or imply that either canonical system is stronger. It records only the absence of a materially matched public canonical comparison cell at the reviewed evidence boundary.
